issues.legal_issue: A conviction entered after reversal of an acquittal is sustainable when the evidence is properly appraised and establishes guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
material_facts: The High Court set aside the trial court’s acquittal and convicted the accused, and the appeal was brought under Section 2(a) of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970.
Two eyewitnesses gave consistent accounts of the assailant and the manner of the shooting.
Their evidence was corroborated by the medical evidence and ballistic evidence linking the recovered cartridges to the accused’s pistol.
The first information report was lodged promptly and contained the account of the occurrence.
The trial court’s acquittal rested on an erroneous appraisal of the evidence and undue emphasis on minor discrepancies.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right to reverse the acquittal and convict the accused under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 27 of the Arms Act; the convictions and sentences were upheld and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 2(a) of the Supreme Court (Enlargement of Appellate Jurisdiction) Act, 1970, the Court independently appraised the evidence. Consistent and reliable eyewitness testimony, supported by medical and ballistic evidence, established the offences under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 27 of the Arms Act beyond reasonable doubt. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: appeal_from_acquittal and consistent_eyewitness_accounts and corroborating_evidence and prompt_account_of_occurrence and acquittal_based_on_misappraisal

predicates.appeal_from_acquittal: The proceeding was an appeal challenging a conviction entered after an earlier acquittal was reversed.
predicates.consistent_eyewitness_accounts: Two eyewitnesses gave consistent accounts of who committed the shooting and how it occurred.
predicates.corroborating_evidence: Medical and ballistic evidence supported the eyewitness accounts and linked the shooting to the accused’s weapon.
predicates.prompt_account_of_occurrence: An account of the occurrence was reported promptly to the authorities.
predicates.acquittal_based_on_misappraisal: The trial court’s acquittal rested on an erroneous assessment of the evidence and undue emphasis on minor discrepancies.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a conviction entered after reversal of an acquittal, consistent eyewitness accounts supported by corroborating evidence and a prompt account of the occurrence, together with an acquittal based on misappraisal, support upholding the convictions.

issues.legal_issue: Semi-digested food in a deceased person’s stomach does not discredit otherwise reliable eyewitness testimony about the approximate time of a meal and a fatal occurrence when the medical timing evidence is inconclusive.
material_facts: The eyewitnesses testified that the deceased ate a meal at about 10:30 a.m. and that the shooting occurred around noon.
The doctor found semi-solid, undigested food in the stomach and stated that digestion begins after about one to one and a half hours.
The doctor did not specify the extent of the undigested food.
The witnesses’ stated times were approximate, and the evidence did not establish the type or amount of food eaten.
The eyewitnesses’ testimony was otherwise reliable.
issues.conclusion: The medical evidence did not contradict or discredit the eyewitnesses’ account of the meal and the time of the occurrence.
issues.legal_principle: Medical evidence about digestion is opinion evidence and is not decisive where digestion varies with the individual and with the type and amount of food, and the medical evidence does not specify the extent of digestion. Approximate timing based on such evidence is not enough to discredit otherwise reliable eyewitness testimony.

rule.if: criminal_homicide_case and approximate_meal_time and digestion_varies and medical_timing_unspecific and eyewitnesses_otherwise_reliable

predicates.criminal_homicide_case: The proceeding concerned a prosecution for a fatal assault.
predicates.approximate_meal_time: The witnesses gave an approximate rather than precisely measured time for the deceased’s meal.
predicates.digestion_varies: The evidence showed that digestion differs among people and depends on the type and amount of food.
predicates.medical_timing_unspecific: The doctor did not specify the extent of undigested food or provide a conclusive time for the meal.
predicates.eyewitnesses_otherwise_reliable: The witnesses’ account was otherwise consistent and reliable.

issues.definition: In a fatal-assault case, approximate meal timing and variable digestion, coupled with unspecific medical timing evidence, do not discredit eyewitnesses whose testimony is otherwise reliable.

issues.legal_issue: A delay in sending cartridges for ballistic examination does not establish substitution when the evidence shows intact seals and untampered custody and no evidential basis for tampering is raised.
material_facts: The sealed packets containing the pistol and cartridges were sent to the ballistic expert after a long delay.
Witnesses who handled the packets testified that they remained sealed and were not tampered with while in their custody.
The ballistic expert testified that the seals were intact and matched the specimen seal.
The relevant custody witnesses were not cross-examined on tampering, and no suggestion of substitution was made to them or to the officer who seized the weapon.
issues.conclusion: There was no basis to find that the cartridges had been substituted, and the ballistic evidence was accepted as corroboration.
issues.legal_principle: A delay in forensic examination may raise a concern about substitution, but that concern is dispelled by evidence that sealed exhibits remained untampered with through custody and arrived with intact seals; an unsupported possibility of substitution does not defeat the evidence.

rule.if: ballistic_evidence_case and delayed_forensic_submission and sealed_packets_intact and untampered_custody_testimony and no_tampering_challenge

predicates.ballistic_evidence_case: The prosecution relied on ballistic examination of recovered cartridges and a weapon.
predicates.delayed_forensic_submission: The sealed exhibits were sent for forensic examination after a substantial delay.
predicates.sealed_packets_intact: The exhibits were reported to have arrived with their seals intact and matching the specimen seal.
predicates.untampered_custody_testimony: People who handled the exhibits testified that they were not tampered with while in their custody.
predicates.no_tampering_challenge: The custody witnesses were not cross-examined on tampering and no suggestion of substitution was put to them or the seizing officer.

issues.definition: In a ballistic-evidence case, delayed forensic submission does not establish cartridge substitution when intact seals, untampered custody testimony, and the absence of a tampering challenge support the exhibits’ integrity.
